subject: Deployment mode follow-up & pricing: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
message_1_subject: Deployment mode follow-up & pricing: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
message_1_body:
Hi Sara —

Great to meet you and Tom earlier. Thanks for walking through Acme's MLPipeline use cases; helpful context. Per our call, I wanted to capture next steps and a short pricing sketch across the three deployment modes you asked about: Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem).

Quick recap of requirements you confirmed:
- High throughput inference for batched prediction jobs (3M tokens/day peak)
- Low-latency interactive features for internal tooling (~200 qps)
- Data residency + SOC 2 compliance for PII-heavy datasets
- Multi-month predictability preferred for budgeting (Q3 commit)

Pricing sketch (ballpark, see attached spreadsheet for numbers):
1) Hosted API: simple per-token + per-request pricing. Good for fast time-to-value and variable traffic. Example: $0.0008 per prompt token / $0.0016 per completion token for curated model. No reserved commit.
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools with monthly commit. Lower per-token cost at scale; recommended if you want predictable throughput for the interactive tier. Example: 2x A100 equivalents reserved ~ $X/month + $0.0005 per token for overflow.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem): license + support + infra ops. Best for strict data residency and air-gapped needs. Upfront platform fee + annual support; OPEX for hardware.

Attachments: I attached a short pricing summary and a starter cost model workbook (acme_cost_model_v1.xlsx) where we can toggle token volumes and commit levels.

Next steps:
- I can run a tailored cost model for your actual token/throughput mix if you share 30-day sample traces or a representative daily profile.
- If you want Dedicated estimates, I’ll loop in Neha (pricing/finance) for commit-level numbers.
- If Private is of interest, we should schedule a technical follow-up with our infra partner (approx 45 min).

Would you prefer I build the model against your 30-day trace or the high/medium/low profile we discussed?

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

+1 415-555-0123

message_3_subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up & pricing: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — tailored cost model
message_3_body:
Hi Sara/Tom —

Thanks for the trace. I ran the model and attached a short summary: redwood_pricing_summary_q2.pdf (tabbed by deployment mode) and acme_cost_model_v1.xlsx (updated). Key takeaways: 

1) Hosted API (variable):
- Estimated monthly cost on your 7-day extrapolated profile: $18k–$22k
- Pros: zero infra ops, immediate rollout. Cons: higher per-token at peak, less predictable.

2) Dedicated capacity (reserved commit):
- Recommend a 3-month commit at 30% headroom vs observed peak. Estimated reserved cost: $12k/month + overflow usage charges. Effective per-token cost drops ~30% vs hosted at your volumes. Break-even vs hosted in ~6–8 weeks given your peak patterns.

3) Private (VPC/on-prem):
- One-time platform + integration estimate: $150k–$220k (depends on on-prem infra) + annual support. Good for strict compliance; longer lead times.

Notes on assumptions: model assumes curated open model variants (Redwood-verified) and 20% KV cache hit rate for batched jobs. I flagged the workbook where you can change cache hit and commit size.

Aditya/Neha — can you confirm the concrete reserved-tier pricing for a 3-month commit at the recommended capacity? If we can get a formal committed quote today, I’ll share a 1-page committed vs variable comparison for Acme and set a follow-up with your finance/purchasing team.

Sara — if this looks directionally right I can produce a 1P slide for Tom with recommended next-step (Dedicated PoC vs Hosted pilot).

Thanks —
Marissa

--
